The Minister of Education, Tunji Alausa, has defended President Bola Tinubu’s academic record at the Chicago State University, insisting that the President graduated with a first-class degree in accounting from the American institution. Alausa said he was familiar with the university, having lived in Chicago for almost 30 years, and had personally met several people who studied with Tinubu. He stated this during an interview on Channels Television on Tuesday while responding to questions about the President’s educational qualifications. “I’m telling you hardcore facts. I lived in Chicago for almost 30 years. I’ve been to that university so many times,” he said. Asked whether he had met Tinubu’s classmates, the minister replied, “Oh, many, many, many, in person. Many. So forget the nonsense of…” When asked whether the President graduated with a first-class degree from the institution, Alausa answered, “In accounting, of course.” He also described Tinubu as a genius, dismissing questions about the President’s intellectual capacity. “Oh, he’s a genius. Let’s not talk about the capability of this President. President Bola Ahmed Tinubu is literally a genius,” he said. Make PUNCH part of your everyday experience. Add us to your Preferred Sources The minister further defended Tinubu’s performance in office, claiming that the President had transformed Nigeria from a moribund country into a growing economy. “Look at how he’s transformed a moribund country three years ago to a country that is growing,” Alausa said. However, when the interviewer challenged the description by pointing to the country’s out-of-school children and poverty levels, the minister insisted that the conversation should remain focused on the President’s achievements. “Let me focus on what you’re saying. I don’t want you to derail this conversation. But this President has delivered this for Nigeria,” he added. The debate resurfaced in August 2026 after the Independent National Electoral Commission began displaying the personal particulars and academic credentials submitted by presidential candidates for the 2027 general elections. Tinubu’s Form EC9, sighted by PUNCH, listed a Bachelor of Science degree in Business Administration from Chicago State University, awarded with honours on June 22, 1979. The form also listed his National Youth Service Corps discharge documents, indicating that he served in Oyo State from December 1982 to November 1983. However, the spaces provided for his primary and secondary school qualifications were entered as “0000”, with only his university qualification indicated in the educational history published by the commission. The development renewed questions about the President’s educational background, with political figures and commentators expressing different views on the omissions. The university had earlier confirmed that Tinubu attended the institution and graduated in 1979, with accounting as his major. In September 2023, the university released Tinubu’s academic records following a legal request by former Vice-President Atiku Abubakar, who sought the documents as part of his challenge to the President’s election victory. The university’s registrar, Caleb Westberg, also testified in a United States court that Tinubu attended and graduated from the institution. However, the university’s records confirm accounting as Tinubu’s major but do not specify that he graduated with a first-class classification. The claim that he obtained a first-class degree was made by Alausa during Tuesday’s interview. In October 2023, a BBC fact-check found no evidence that Tinubu forged the Chicago State University diploma he submitted to INEC.
